RuleEventRef.description:
A pointer to one raw event behind a rule hit (the teacher's replay, rule #6).

`at` is the event's trusted time (`server_ts`, else `client_ts`) — exactly the
`at` of the dashboard's timeline entry, so a rule card can jump to it.
RuleEventRef.title: RuleEventRef

events.description: Raw events behind the hit (bounded list).
events.title: Events

item_ids.description: Questions / writing items the hit rests on.
item_ids.title: Item Ids

RuleHit.description: One deterministic integrity rule that fired, with its numbers spelled out.

explanation_ru.description: Russian sentence built from the actual numbers of this attempt.
explanation_ru.title: Explanation Ru

title_ru.description: Short Russian title for the teacher.
title_ru.title: Title Ru

RuleHit.title: RuleHit

WritingAssessment.description:
Advisory likelihood that ONE writing answer was produced with outside help.

Outside help = ChatGPT / translator / text copied from another device or tab /
dictation. Advisory only: no score, never moves a grade (golden rule #2).

signals.description: The evidence tags the judgment rests on.
signals.title: Signals

WritingAssessment.title: WritingAssessment

description:
The advisory integrity verdict stored next to (never inside) the grade.

The deterministic rule engine is the verdict of record: `suspicion_score`,
`confidence`, `rules`, `flags` and `summary` come from `app/integrity/rules.py`
and never from a model. An LLM (when `ANALYSIS_LLM=writing`) only adds a second
opinion on the WRITING items: then `model_id` is set and `writing[]` holds its
per-item assessments (floored by the deterministic evidence).

confidence.description: How complete the telemetry behind the rules was.
confidence.title: Confidence

error.description: Why the LLM second opinion is missing (`<ExceptionType>: message`); the rule-engine verdict itself is unaffected.
error.title: Error

input_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the inputs this verdict was computed from (event count, last event id, digest of the analysis context), set by the results layer. An automatic retry reuses a stored LLM verdict whose fingerprint still matches instead of paying for the same analysis again. Not evidence; never shown.
input_fingerprint.title: Input Fingerprint

model_id.description: LLM id of the WRITING second opinion, for auditability. None = no LLM was used: `writing[]` is then the rule engine's own per-item assessment.
model_id.title: Model Id

rules.description: The deterministic rules that fired, strongest first.
rules.title: Rules

rules_version.description: Version of the rule engine that produced `rules` / `suspicion_score`. None = a verdict stored before the rule engine existed (its suspicion came from the old formula or from an LLM; a regrade recomputes it).
rules_version.title: Rules Version

suspicion_score.description: Rule-engine suspicion (bounded combination of the hits).
suspicion_score.title: Suspicion Score

title: AnalysisVerdict
